definition: The specific case where a motion's start or stop is caused by an external force or object contact (a wall, a spring, a trigger discharge) rather than the moving thing's own effort — such a transition should be abrupt/near-instant rather than eased, because the physical cause of the change is itself abrupt.
purpose: Keep an externally-caused stop or start reading as caused by that external event, rather than contradicting it with a self-generated-looking gradual ease.
visible_effect: A hard, immediate transition into or out of a pose at the exact moment of the external event (a collision, a trigger pull, a spring release), with no gradual ramp on that side of the transition, even though the SAME object's self-powered motion elsewhere may ease normally.
psychological_or_gameplay_effect: An eased stop against a wall reads as if the object slowed itself down on purpose, contradicting the read of a hard collision; an eased launch out of a spring or a gun reads as self-powered effort rather than an instantaneous external force, undercutting the whole point of showing that force.
physical_interpretation: A direct physical distinction: slow-in/slow-out approximates a body's own acceleration under its own force, but a sudden EXTERNAL force (impact, discharge, release) genuinely does change velocity abruptly in reality, so an abrupt transition is the physically correct choice here, not an exception to physical accuracy.
use_cases: a character or object colliding with a solid surface, ending self-powered easing on impact
a launch caused by an external mechanism (a spring, a cannon, an explosion) rather than the object's own effort
a weapon discharge (a gunshot, a released bowstring) whose kick or release reads as sudden specifically because nothing eases into it
non_use_cases: the SAME object's own self-powered acceleration/deceleration elsewhere in the same motion, which should still ease normally — this rule applies only at the moment an external force takes over, not to the whole motion
a soft or cushioned impact where the collision itself is not abrupt (landing in water, a padded surface), where the physical premise of a hard stop does not hold
interactions: Slow in/slow out — this is the specific exception to it, not a separate principle; both existing non_use_cases in that card describe when a smooth ease is inappropriate for STYLE reasons, while this one is about PHYSICAL CAUSE instead
Timing — the moment of external contact is exactly the kind of event `ai/events.js`'s shot-event timeline exists to mark
Recovery-weight substitution / startup frame budget — a sibling case of the same broader idea that not every transition should default to a smooth, self-generated-looking curve

style_variations.mechanical: a related but distinct case — mechanical style removes easing from SELF-powered motion by convention; this entry removes it specifically at an EXTERNAL-force moment, on any style, including ones that ease everywhere else

cadence_representation: Not represented as a distinct rule, though fully expressible with existing tools: `set_easing` already supports a stepped/abrupt style at a specific key (named under the existing `slow_in_slow_out` card), so nothing NEW needs to be built to apply this — what is missing is the RULE that tells a caller WHEN to reach for it (an external-force event) versus when a smooth ease is still correct on the very same track.
control_surface: `set_easing` at the key coinciding with the external-force event; `ai/events.js` markers to identify which key that is.
detection_and_measurement_methods: Partially measurable: `ai/motion.js` already measures the actual acceleration curve at any key, so a mismatch — an eased-in transition at a key that is ALSO marked as a contact/impact event — is detectable by cross-referencing existing easing data against existing contact/event markers; nothing in this build currently runs that specific cross-reference.
generation_or_modification_methods: `set_easing` changes the easing style/direction at an existing key; nothing decides automatically which keys are external-force moments requiring it.
failure_modes: an eased stop against a solid collision, which reads as the object slowing itself down rather than being stopped by the wall
an eased launch out of a spring or weapon discharge, which undercuts the instantaneousness that sells the force of the mechanism
over-applying this rule to a soft or cushioned impact that was never physically abrupt to begin with
roblox_considerations: None specific — a pure keyframe-easing concept independent of the target engine.
examples: Sonic's own acceleration/deceleration eases normally, but hitting a wall stops him instantly and a spring launches him instantly — both external-force moments named directly and contrasted against his self-powered movement (video 5 @ 4:26–4:48)
a gunshot's kick reading as correct specifically because there is no slow-out into that initial pose — "it's just instant kick" (video 5 @ 4:48–4:58)
evidence_status: video: https://youtu.be/3jNiNctcQ4c @ 4:26–4:58 — Dan contrasts Sonic's self-powered easing against his instant stop/launch on external contact (Sonic's running and a nearby spring/bumper object confirmed on screen at t=4:34–4:44), and separately names a gunshot's instant kick as the same rule; experimental until validated
